scope: Browser guide interactions and mocked native GitHub OAuth IPC only
checks: A fresh profile opens the first-use guide with clear progress and a skip action
Browser sign-in is explicitly a desktop feature and requests no token
Practice teaches file selection, a named local commit, and an explicitly simulated push
Completing the guide keeps local work available and remembers the choice after reload
The guide can be replayed from both the command palette and A little help
Escape closes the account guide and returns keyboard focus to its launcher
Every guide step remains usable at 320px and 390px with reduced motion
A build without an OAuth Client ID still supports the guide and local work
Sign-in shows a one-time code, opens the trusted backend browser action, and cancels cleanly
Mocked consent connects the account across the interface and disconnect removes it
Denied, expired, and interrupted consent give retry guidance and preserve local access
A late successful poll cannot reconnect the interface after cancellation
Pending consent respects its polling interval and GitHub slow-down postpones the next request
Publishing requires connected GitHub, autofills author identity, and sends no GitHub credential through IPC
Guide and mocked consent produce no browser errors or real provider requests
